title: Which layer stops it?
brief: Five commands. Before each one runs, say which layer you expect to stop it: the floor refuses it before anyone is asked, a card asks you first, or it runs without a card. Then watch what the real check does. Try the dangerous ones — nothing runs here, ever.

beats.say: Delete a folder and everything in it.
beats.debrief: rm -rf is on the floor in any flag order. The floor is code: no config file, plan or card can let it through.

beats.say: Download a script and run it straight away.
beats.debrief: Piping a download into a shell runs code nobody has read. The floor refuses that shape.

beats.say: Look at what has changed in a project.
beats.debrief: Reading the state of a project changes nothing, so it is on the free list and runs without a card.

beats.say: Overwrite the shared copy of a project with this one.
beats.debrief: Not on the floor and not on the free list, so a card asks. A force push can throw away other people's work: read it before you press.

beats.say: The same download, saved to a file first and then run.
beats.debrief: Rephrased, the download-and-run slips past the floor's pattern — but a chained command always asks. The card is the boundary when a pattern misses.
